text.p: Economic indicators show that the fundamentals of the Japanese economy are improving, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said in a speech on Thursday.
Mitsuzuka said the government's monthly economic report, issued on Tuesday, showed that the economy was gradually but steadily growing.
"The fact that individual indicators are improving shows that economic fundamentals have become more solid," Mitsuzuka said.
He added that overall, not only the government but also private analysts believed the economy was becoming steadier.
On the issue of recent falls in Tokyo stock prices, Mitsuzuka said the basic principle was to "ask the market about market matters".
He reiterated that swift enactment of the supplementary budget for the current fiscal year and the state budget for 1997/98, starting on April 1, was important.
